name: The Fool
meaning_up: New beginnings, innocence, spontaneity, faith in the unknown
meaning_rev: Recklessness, risk-taking, inconsideration, foolish decisions
description: The Fool represents new beginnings, having faith in the future, being inexperienced, not knowing what to expect, and having beginners luck.
detailed_description: The Fool is the first card of the Major Arcana, symbolizing the beginning of a spiritual journey and life itself. Depicted as a carefree young person with minimal baggage, ready to step off a cliff's edge, this card speaks of innocence, trust, and the courage to start something new without the burden of the past or worry about the future. The Fool invites us to have faith that the universe will support our steps, even when we don't have a map. This is about surrendering to life's experiences and trusting the process. In its reversed position, The Fool warns against recklessness, unnecessary risk-taking, and failing to consider consequences.

name: The Magician
meaning_up: Willpower, desire, creation, manifestation, resourcefulness
meaning_rev: Trickery, illusions, out of touch, manipulation, misuse of power
description: The Magician has all the tools needed to manifest his desires and achieve his goals through willpower and skill.
detailed_description: The Magician is a figure who bridges heaven and earth, representing willpower and the ability to turn ideas into reality. With one hand pointing upward (receiving inspiration from the spiritual realm) and the other pointing downward (manifesting into the physical realm), he is a channel of creative energy. On his table are symbols of the four Tarot suits (Cups, Swords, Wands, Pentacles), representing mastery over various life elements: emotions, thoughts, spirituality, and material matters. This card is about concentration, skill, and maximizing available resources. The Magician reminds us that we possess all the tools needed for success. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate manipulation, illusions, or misuse of power.

name: The High Priestess
meaning_up: Intuition, unconscious knowledge, divine feminine, mystery, inner wisdom
meaning_rev: Secrets, disconnected from intuition, withdrawal, blocked inner voice
description: The High Priestess represents intuition, the subconscious mind, and spiritual wisdom that comes from within.
detailed_description: The High Priestess is the guardian of the subconscious and divine mysteries. Seated between two pillars (Boaz and Jakin, symbols of duality such as conscious and unconscious), she holds the Torah scroll and has a crescent moon at her feet. She represents quiet wisdom, intuitive knowledge not taught in schools, and the mysterious feminine side. This card invites us to listen to our inner voice, trust our hunches, and delve into the world of dreams and symbols. The High Priestess is the gateway to deeper self-understanding and universal wisdom. She is not about intellectual knowledge but about 'knowing' without needing reasons. In its reversed position, she may indicate rejection of intuition, hidden secrets, or inability to access inner wisdom.

name: The Empress
meaning_up: Femininity, beauty, nature, nurturing, abundance, creative fertility
meaning_rev: Creative block, dependence, smothering, lack of growth
description: The Empress represents feminine power, creativity, nature, abundance, and nurturing energy.
detailed_description: The Empress is the embodiment of the feminine principle in its most fertile and creative form. She is Mother Nature seated in a lush, fruitful landscape, symbolizing fertility, beauty, and abundance. She represents creativity giving birth to something new—whether art, business, or life itself (such as pregnancy). Her energy is about nurturing, unconditional acceptance, and sensory enjoyment. The Empress encourages us to connect with nature, care for ourselves and others, and appreciate the beauty around us. She is the source of all things that grow and flourish. In its reversed meaning, she may indicate blocked creativity, unhealthy dependence, or excessive nurturing that becomes suffocating.

name: The Emperor
meaning_up: Authority, structure, control, stability, fatherhood, leadership
meaning_rev: Domination, excessive control, rigidity, tyranny, inflexibility
description: The Emperor represents structure, authority, rules, and power that comes from discipline and organization.
detailed_description: The Emperor is the figure of authority, structure, and order. As the counterpart to The Empress, he represents the masculine principle—logic, discipline, and control. Seated on a stone throne with a royal scepter, he is the lawmaker and protector of the realm. This card speaks of the importance of strong foundations, decisive leadership, and responsibility. The Emperor builds the world through rules, strategy, and clear hierarchies. He is the father who provides security and boundaries. This card encourages us to take control of our lives, set clear goals, and act with discipline. In its reversed position, his power may turn into tyranny, rigidity, or inability to lead fairly.

name: The Hierophant
meaning_up: Tradition, conformity, morality, ethics, spiritual guidance, established systems
meaning_rev: Rebellion, subversiveness, new approaches, personal spirituality
description: The Hierophant represents traditional values, spiritual wisdom, education, and conformity to established systems.
detailed_description: The Hierophant (or The High Priest) is the bridge between the divine and society. He represents traditional institutions, religion, belief systems, and established social conventions. Standing between two church pillars, he bestows blessings and spiritual teachings to his two followers. This card speaks of seeking meaning through existing structures, such as schools, religion, or traditional mentors. It's about ritual, morality, and collective wisdom passed down through generations. The Hierophant offers spiritual guidance and a sense of belonging to a community. In its reversed meaning, he may indicate rebellion against dogma, rejection of traditional authority, or the search for a more personal and unconventional spiritual path.

name: The Lovers
meaning_up: Love, harmony, relationships, choices, alignment of values, partnership
meaning_rev: Imbalance, misalignment, disharmony, conflict in relationships
description: The Lovers represent relationships, choices, and alignment of values, often indicating important decisions about love.
detailed_description: The Lovers represents more than just romantic love; it's about unity, choices, and alignment of values. This card often depicts Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden with an angel above, signifying the relationship between humanity and the divine, as well as between humans. It's about attraction, deep connection, and important decisions that determine our life path. The Lovers invite us to choose with our hearts, seek harmony, and align our actions with our deepest values and desires. It may represent significant relationships, partnerships, or even the 'marriage' between different aspects within ourselves. In its reversed position, this indicates misalignment, conflict in relationships, or choices made based on poor judgment.

name: The Chariot
meaning_up: Control, willpower, success, action, determination, overcoming obstacles
meaning_rev: Lack of control, aggression, directionless, internal conflict
description: The Chariot represents willpower, determination, and the ability to overcome obstacles through focused effort.
detailed_description: The Chariot is the card of victory through strong determination and self-control. A charioteer stands in a war chariot, pulled by two sphinxes or horses of contrasting colors (black and white), symbolizing opposing forces that must be directed and controlled. With his reigns and will, he unifies these forces to move forward toward his goal. This card speaks of ambition, focus, and the ability to overcome obstacles with mental strength. The journey may be challenging, but self-control and unwavering determination will bring success. This is the energy of conquest and achievement. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate lack of direction, loss of control, aggression, or conflicting forces pulling us in different directions.

name: Strength
meaning_up: Inner strength, courage, patience, compassion, control, resilience
meaning_rev: Self-doubt, weakness, insecurity, fear, lack of control
description: Strength represents inner fortitude, courage, patience, and the ability to tame one's inner beasts through compassion.
detailed_description: Strength in Tarot is not about brute physical force, but rather inner strength, moral courage, and resilience of spirit. This card typically depicts a woman gently closing the mouth of a lion, symbolizing the taming of animal instincts, fear, and anger through compassion and self-control. The flowers in her hair and around the lion indicate gentleness and connection with nature. This card teaches that true strength comes from self-confidence, patience, and compassion—both toward oneself and others. It's about having a courageous heart to face life's challenges with calmness and confidence. In its reversed position, it indicates self-doubt, weakness, fear taking over, or inappropriate use of power.

name: The Hermit
meaning_up: Soul-searching, introspection, being alone, inner guidance, wisdom
meaning_rev: Isolation, loneliness, withdrawal, lost direction
description: The Hermit represents introspection, solitude, and the search for inner wisdom through withdrawal from the world.
detailed_description: The Hermit is the seeker of wisdom who leaves the crowd to journey within. With his simple cloak, staff, and lantern illuminating the path through darkness, he symbolizes the search for meaning, self-knowledge, and spiritual truth. His solitude is a choice for reflection and contemplation. This card appears when we need to retreat from external noise to listen to our inner voice, seek answers from within, or gain clarity about life's purpose. The Hermit may also represent a teacher or spiritual mentor appearing in our lives. In its reversed meaning, solitude may turn into painful isolation, withdrawal from society, or inability to find the answers sought.

name: Wheel of Fortune
meaning_up: Good luck, karma, life cycles, turning point, destiny, change
meaning_rev: Bad luck, resistance to change, breaking cycles, stagnation
description: The Wheel of Fortune represents cycles, fate, change, and the turning points in life that are beyond our control.
detailed_description: The Wheel of Fortune is the universal symbol of life cycles, destiny, and inevitable change. The continuously turning wheel raises those below and lowers those above, reminding us that life is a series of ups and downs. Around the wheel often appear mystical figures (such as Sphinx, Anubis, Typhon) and inscriptions like 'Tarot', 'Rota', 'Tora', 'Ator', signifying cosmic law and destiny. This card marks moments of major change, turning points, or shifting luck. It's about understanding and accepting life's natural rhythms, karma, and how everything is interconnected. As the wheel turns, we're invited to be flexible and trust the process. In its reversed position, it may indicate resistance to change, cycles of bad luck, or instability.

name: Justice
meaning_up: Justice, fairness, truth, cause and effect, accountability, legal matters
meaning_rev: Unfairness, dishonesty, lack of accountability, injustice
description: Justice represents fairness, truth, and the consequences of our actions, emphasizing balance and accountability.
detailed_description: Justice sits on a throne with a sword in one hand (symbolizing clear thinking and truth) and scales in the other (symbolizing balance and fair decisions). This card is the embodiment of the law of cause and effect (karma), absolute justice, and truth. It reminds us that every action has consequences, and ultimately balance will be restored. Justice appears in readings related to legal decisions, contracts, or situations where fairness and honesty are paramount. On a personal level, it encourages us to take responsibility for our choices, seek truth, and act with integrity. In its reversed meaning, it indicates injustice, dishonesty, prejudice, or refusal to take responsibility.

name: The Hanged Man
meaning_up: Surrender, new perspective, enlightenment, letting go, pause
meaning_rev: Stalling, resistance, martyrdom, stubbornness
description: The Hanged Man represents surrender, suspension, and seeing things from a new perspective through letting go.
detailed_description: The Hanged Man is one of the most paradoxical cards. He's depicted hanging upside down from one foot with a peaceful and accepting face, often with a halo of light around his head. This position is not about punishment, but rather about voluntary sacrifice, surrender, and gaining a new perspective by 'seeing the world upside down'. This card invites us to stop struggling, accept a pause or uncertainty, and find wisdom in stillness. It's a time for reflection, short-term sacrifice for long-term gain, and radical shifts in perspective. The Hanged Man is about enlightenment through suspension. In its reversed position, surrender may turn into stagnation, refusal to see things in new ways, or feeling like a martyr.

name: Death
meaning_up: Endings, change, transformation, transition, renewal, closure
meaning_rev: Resistance to change, stagnation, fear of letting go, delay
description: Death represents transformation, endings, and new beginnings, signifying profound change and renewal.
detailed_description: Don't be afraid of the Death card—it rarely means physical death. Instead, it's the card of the most profound change and transformation. Death as a figure riding a white horse often carries a banner with a rose, symbolizing the end of one cycle and the beginning of another. The background often shows a sunrise between two pillars, symbolizing hope and renewal. This card indicates that something in our lives (habits, relationships, jobs, phases) must end for something new to be born. This process may feel like 'death' because it involves release and endings, but it's essential for growth. Death is about radical transformation and spiritual renewal. In its reversed meaning, it indicates resistance to inevitable change, stagnation, or fear of letting go.

name: Temperance
meaning_up: Balance, moderation, patience, purpose, harmony, blending opposites
meaning_rev: Imbalance, excess, lack of harmony, impatience
description: Temperance represents balance, moderation, and the harmonious blending of opposites to create something new.
detailed_description: Temperance is an angel calmly pouring liquid between two cups, symbolizing the harmonious blending of opposites to create something new and better. With one foot in water (emotions, subconscious) and one on land (reality, consciousness), she is the guardian of balance. This card speaks of moderation, patience, adjustment, and finding the perfect 'middle way'. Temperance invites us to manage our energy and resources wisely, combining different aspects of our lives (such as work and rest, or logic and intuition) harmoniously. It's also about healing, adaptation, and acting with clear yet flexible purpose. In its reversed position, it indicates imbalance, excess, disharmony, or impatience.

name: The Devil
meaning_up: Addiction, materialism, playfulness, bondage, temptation, shadow aspects
meaning_rev: Freedom, release, reclaiming power, breaking chains
description: The Devil represents bondage, addiction, materialism, and the shadow aspects of our nature that hold us back.
detailed_description: The Devil symbolizes bondage, temptation, and the shadow aspects of human nature. The classic image is a goat-like figure (Baphomet) with a pair of humans (Adam and Eve) chained, but the chains are loose—indicating that this bondage is often an illusion or choice. This card speaks of attachments to material things, addictions (whether substances, work, relationships, or thought patterns), and self-imposed limitations. The Devil reveals areas where we feel powerless, controlled by desires, or trapped in destructive patterns. It asks us to recognize our chains and understand that the key to freedom is in our hands. In its reversed meaning, this is a card of liberation, release from bonds, and reclaiming personal power.

name: The Tower
meaning_up: Sudden change, disruption, awakening, release, shocking truth
meaning_rev: Avoiding disaster, fear of change, delaying the inevitable
description: The Tower represents sudden upheaval, destruction of old structures, and the shocking revelation of truth.
detailed_description: The Tower is the card of drastic, destructive yet liberating change. A tower built on fragile foundations is struck by lightning, fire blazes, and two people fall. This symbolizes the sudden collapse of structures, beliefs, or situations in our lives that are no longer stable or true. Though frightening, this destruction is necessary to shatter illusions, lies, or arrogant ego structures. The Tower clears the way for something new and more authentic. It's a 'shocking revelation' that forces us to see the truth. The process may be painful, but it brings enlightenment and liberation in the end. In its reversed position, it may indicate that drastic change is being avoided (only delaying the inevitable) or that its impact is somewhat milder.

name: The Star
meaning_up: Hope, faith, rejuvenation, inspiration, serenity, healing, guidance
meaning_rev: Discouragement, insecurity, lack of faith, hopelessness
description: The Star represents hope, inspiration, and spiritual guidance after a period of darkness or difficulty.
detailed_description: After the storm of The Tower comes The Star—the card of hope, healing, and divine inspiration. A young woman pours water from two jugs into a river and onto the land, nourishing the earth and reconnecting it with the subconscious (water). Her main bright star (often eight-pointed) in the sky provides guidance and faith. This card speaks of spiritual recovery, rediscovering life purpose, and having calm faith that things will get better. It's a time for healing wounds, contemplating dreams, and connecting with our inner source of inspiration. The Star brings a message of optimism, serenity, and trust in the future. In its reversed meaning, it indicates discouragement, loss of faith, feeling disconnected from spiritual guidance, or unrealistic hopes.

name: The Moon
meaning_up: Illusion, fear, subconscious, intuition, dreams, hidden aspects
meaning_rev: Release of fear, repressed emotion, misunderstanding, clarity
description: The Moon represents illusion, the subconscious mind, dreams, and the hidden aspects of ourselves.
detailed_description: The Moon takes us into the realm of dreams, illusions, and the subconscious. The dim moonlight creates shadows and distortions, making it difficult to distinguish reality from fear. A wolf and a dog howl, and a lobster (or crab) emerges from the water, representing animal instincts and subconscious content rising to the surface. This card marks a time of confusion, uncertainty, or facing hidden fears and anxieties. It invites us to explore our shadow side, trust our intuition even when things aren't rational, and understand that not everything seen is real. The journey under moonlight can be frightening but is necessary for growth. In its reversed position, it may mean facing and releasing fears, clarifying confusion, or repressed emotions finally being acknowledged.

name: The Sun
meaning_up: Joy, success, celebration, positivity, vitality, happiness, achievement
meaning_rev: Temporary depression, lack of success, blocked happiness
description: The Sun represents joy, success, vitality, and the radiant energy that brings warmth and happiness.
detailed_description: The Sun is the most positive and joyful card in Tarot. Its bright sunlight illuminates everything with clarity and truth, opposite to The Moon's illusions. A young child rides a white horse under sunflowers, symbolizing innocence, joy, and freedom. This card means success, achievement, vitality, and recognition. It brings energy of optimism, confidence, and simple life joy. Everything grows and flourishes under the sun. The Sun marks a period of happiness, good health, and goal realization. It is illumination and understanding after dark times. In its reversed position, joy may be temporary, blocked, or not fully realized, but generally remains a positive card.

name: Judgement
meaning_up: Judgment, rebirth, inner calling, absolution, awakening, higher purpose
meaning_rev: Self-doubt, refusal of call, fear of judgment, delay
description: Judgment represents awakening, rebirth, and the calling to a higher purpose or spiritual mission.
detailed_description: Judgement depicts the day of spiritual awakening. An angel (often Gabriel) blows a trumpet, and people rise from their graves with arms raised, ready to be judged and reborn. This is not about frightening external judgment, but rather about a moment of personal awakening, self-assessment, and answering life's 'call' to a higher purpose. This card marks a turning point where we reflect on our lives, forge a new identity, and free ourselves from the past. It's about forgiveness (especially for oneself), redemption, and making important decisions aligned with our soul's purpose. Judgement calls us to wake up and live more authentically. In its reversed position, it indicates refusal of this call, self-doubt, fear of being judged, or refusal to face the past.

name: The World
meaning_up: Completion, integration, accomplishment, travel, wholeness, fulfillment
meaning_rev: Lack of closure, fear of completion, delays, incompleteness
description: The World represents completion, wholeness, achievement, and the successful conclusion of a cycle.
detailed_description: The World is the final card of the Major Arcana, symbolizing completion, success, and total integration. An androgynous dancer (often surrounded by an oval wreath) holds two wands, surrounded by four creatures at the corners (human, lion, bull, eagle—symbols of the four evangelists and the four elements). This represents the unification of all lessons from the previous journey. This card marks the achievement of a major goal, a feeling of wholeness, and awareness of our place in the universe. It is the successful end of a cycle and preparation to begin a new one (returning to The Fool). The World is also associated with travel, especially extensive journeys, and satisfying worldly experiences. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate slight delays in achievement, a sense of incompleteness, or fear of taking the final step.

name: Ace of Wands
meaning_up: Inspiration, new opportunities, growth, potential, creative spark
meaning_rev: Delays, lack of motivation, missed opportunities, creative block
description: The Ace of Wands represents new inspiration, creative potential, and the spark of an exciting new venture.
detailed_description: The Ace of Wands is the beginning card of the Wands suit (Fire), symbolizing an initial burst of creative energy, inspiration, and potential. A large wand, often with leaves growing from it, is held by a hand emerging from a cloud, offering new opportunity. This is the 'spark' of inspiration, the urge to start a new project, business, or spiritual journey. Its energy is passionate, enthusiastic, and promises growth. This card encourages taking action based on that inspiration. In its reversed meaning, that spark may be extinguished or delayed—lack of motivation, blocked inspiration, or missed opportunities due to hesitation.

name: Two of Wands
meaning_up: Planning, future planning, discovery, decisions, strategic vision
meaning_rev: Fear of unknown, lack of planning, bad decisions, hesitation
description: The Two of Wands represents planning for the future, making decisions, and considering long-term goals.
detailed_description: In the Two of Wands, a figure (often depicted as a ruler or explorer) holds one wand and gazes into the distance, with a second wand attached to the wall behind him. He stands between the known world (palace/castle) and the unexplored world (ocean and mountains). This card represents the planning stage after the initial Ace inspiration. It's about making strategic decisions, considering options, and mapping the future. There's energy of anticipation and desire for expansion. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate fear of the unknown, lack of planning leading to poor decisions, or reluctance to leave the comfort zone.

name: Three of Wands
meaning_up: Expansion, foresight, overseas opportunities, progress, seeing fruits of labor
meaning_rev: Obstacles, delays, frustration, lack of foresight, setbacks
description: The Three of Wands represents expansion, foresight, and seeing your efforts begin to bear fruit.
detailed_description: The Three of Wands continues the journey. Now the figure stands on a high cliff, with three wands erected beside him, watching ships sail on the vast ocean. This symbolizes expansion, progress, and long-term vision. Initial efforts are beginning to show results, and the world opens up with opportunities, possibly involving trade, travel, or long-distance collaboration. This card speaks of having the insight to see future potential and acting on it. It's a sign of optimism and steady growth. In its reversed position, progress may be hindered by obstacles, delays, frustration, or lack of long-term vision.

name: Four of Wands
meaning_up: Celebration, harmony, home, community, marriage, foundation
meaning_rev: Lack of support, home conflicts, instability, disrupted celebrations
description: The Four of Wands represents celebration, harmony, and the joy of coming together in community.
detailed_description: The Four of Wands is a card of joy, stability, and celebration. It often depicts garlands adorning four sturdy wands, with people rejoicing in the foreground and a secure home/castle in the distance. This represents achieving an important milestone, wedding celebrations, housewarming, or simply a moment of happiness and harmony with loved ones. It's about strong foundations, sense of belonging, and enjoyment of the fruits of hard work. In its reversed meaning, celebrations may be delayed or disrupted by family conflicts, lack of support, or a feeling of instability at home.

name: Five of Wands
meaning_up: Conflict, competition, disagreement, rivalry, healthy competition
meaning_rev: Avoiding conflict, inner conflict, resolution, compromise
description: The Five of Wands represents conflict, competition, and the challenges of working with others.
detailed_description: The Five of Wands shows five people fighting or competing with their wands, often in apparent chaos. This symbolizes conflict, competition, disagreements, and friction. This conflict may not be destructive (as in Swords), but rather healthy competition, heated debate, or challenges in teamwork. It may represent a period where many have different ideas and finding agreement is difficult. This card encourages overcoming this competition and finding ways to work together. In its reversed meaning, it may mean avoiding necessary conflict, inner conflict, or the beginning of resolution from disputes.

name: Six of Wands
meaning_up: Victory, success, public recognition, progress, achievement
meaning_rev: Failure, lack of recognition, ego issues, pride
description: The Six of Wands represents victory, success, and recognition for your achievements.
detailed_description: The Six of Wands is a card of victory and public recognition. A winner, riding a horse and holding a wand with a victory garland, is welcomed and praised by the crowd. This symbolizes success after the struggle (Five of Wands). Your efforts, leadership, or talents are recognized by others. It brings feelings of pride, achievement, and progress. This card often appears related to promotions, awards, or success in competitions. In its reversed position, victory may not be achieved, recognition is withheld, or an overly large ego may become problematic.

name: Seven of Wands
meaning_up: Challenge, competition, perseverance, defense, standing ground
meaning_rev: Giving up, overwhelmed, defensive, doubt
description: The Seven of Wands represents standing your ground, defending your position, and perseverance against challenges.
detailed_description: In the Seven of Wands, a figure stands on high ground, holding one wand to defend against six others coming from below. This is a card about standing firm, defending your position, and fighting against challenges or competitors. You may feel criticized, challenged, or forced to defend your opinions or achievements. This card requires determination, courage, and belief in the value of your position. It's about resistance and persistence. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate giving up under pressure, feeling overwhelmed by challenges, or becoming overly defensive and paranoid.

name: Eight of Wands
meaning_up: Speed, action, rapid progress, movement, air travel, swift communication
meaning_rev: Delays, frustration, holding back, waiting, blockage
description: The Eight of Wands represents rapid movement, swift action, and things happening quickly.
detailed_description: The Eight of Wands depicts eight wands flying through the air at high speed, often heading in the same direction. This is a card of quick movement, sudden progress, and accelerated action. Everything previously stalled is now moving at full speed. This could mean travel (especially by air), rapid communication, fast development in projects, or important news arriving quickly. Its energy is dynamic and straight to the point. In its reversed position, this speed is hindered—delays, frustration, communication blockages, or reluctance to move forward.

name: Nine of Wands
meaning_up: Resilience, persistence, last stand, courage, endurance
meaning_rev: Exhaustion, giving up, defensiveness, burnout
description: The Nine of Wands represents resilience, persistence, and the strength to continue despite challenges.
detailed_description: The Nine of Wands shows a tired and wounded figure, leaning on their wand, with eight other wands standing behind them like a fence. They are alert, as if waiting for one final challenge. This card symbolizes resilience, determination, and courage to continue despite having been through many battles. You may feel tired but still have the strength to persist. It's about defense, vigilance, and determination not to give up. This is the last line of defense before victory (moving toward Ten of Wands). In its reversed meaning, exhaustion may be too great, leading to giving up, or excessive defensiveness that hinders progress.

name: Ten of Wands
meaning_up: Burden, responsibility, hard work, stress, completion of tasks
meaning_rev: Release of burden, simplification, dropping responsibilities, delegation
description: The Ten of Wands represents burden, responsibility, and carrying too much weight on your shoulders.
detailed_description: The Ten of Wands depicts a figure struggling to walk, carrying ten large wands that block their view. This is a card of burden, excessive responsibility, and stress. You may feel overwhelmed by the amount of work, commitments, or pressure. Although this indicates completion of a project or task (as number 10 symbolizes completeness), the achievement feels heavy and exhausting. This card asks you to evaluate whether you're carrying too much alone and whether you need to delegate or release some responsibilities. In its reversed meaning, it represents release of that burden—simplifying life, delegating, or finally completing a task that has been weighing you down.

name: Page of Wands
meaning_up: Enthusiasm, exploration, free spirit, discovery, creative energy
meaning_rev: Lack of direction, procrastination, pessimism, scattered energy
description: The Page of Wands represents enthusiasm, exploration, and the energy of new creative ventures.
detailed_description: The Page of Wands is the messenger or student of the Fire element. He stands in the desert with his wand, looking at it with wonder and enthusiasm. He represents news about a creative opportunity, the beginning of a new adventure, or a burst of youthful enthusiasm. His energy is passionate, curious, and spontaneous. This could be someone in your life or an aspect of yourself that is excited to start something new, full of fresh ideas and optimism. In its reversed position, this enthusiasm may be hindered by lack of direction, procrastination, or pessimism that dampens the spirit.

name: Knight of Wands
meaning_up: Action, adventure, impulsiveness, free spirit, passionate pursuit
meaning_rev: Haste, scattered energy, delays, frustration, recklessness
description: The Knight of Wands represents action, adventure, and charging forward with passion and energy.
detailed_description: The Knight of Wands is the passionate and impulsive rider of the Fire suit. In his armor and with his wand, he's ready to charge forward, his horse leaping with energy. He represents quick action, adventure, and the desire to explore new things. He is enthusiastic, brave, and sometimes reckless. His energy can bring fast movement and progress, but it can also be too hasty and disregard consequences. This could be a charismatic and adventurous person, or the drive within to act immediately on dreams. In its reversed meaning, this energy becomes chaotic—rushed, scattered energy, frustration due to delays, or impulsive actions causing problems.

name: Queen of Wands
meaning_up: Confidence, determination, vibrancy, warmth, charisma, creative expression
meaning_rev: Jealousy, insecurity, selfishness, demanding nature, dominance
description: The Queen of Wands represents confidence, charisma, and the warmth of creative self-expression.
detailed_description: The Queen of Wands is the confident and charismatic ruler of the Fire element. Seated on her throne with a wand in one hand and a sunflower in the other, surrounded by a black cat (symbol of mystery and independence), she radiates warmth, charm, and creativity. She is a natural inspirational leader, passionate about her projects, and has magnetic self-confidence. She represents someone independent, expressive, and with a high passion for life. In its reversed meaning, her positive qualities may turn into jealousy, hidden insecurity, selfishness, or becoming too demanding and dominant.

name: King of Wands
meaning_up: Leadership, vision, entrepreneur, honor, charismatic authority
meaning_rev: Impulsiveness, ruthlessness, high expectations, tyranny
description: The King of Wands represents visionary leadership, entrepreneurial spirit, and charismatic authority.
detailed_description: The King of Wands is the supreme visionary and passionate ruler of the Fire suit. Seated on his throne with his wand and salamander (mythical creature living in fire) on his robe, he is a natural leader, entrepreneur, and creator. He has great vision, the ability to inspire others, and the courage to take calculated risks. His authority comes from charisma and vision, not from force or control. He is fair and passionate. In its reversed position, this vision may become impulsive and unrealistic, his leadership may turn cruel and manipulative, or his too-high expectations may become unfair.

name: Ace of Cups
meaning_up: New feelings, spirituality, intuition, love, compassion, emotional opening
meaning_rev: Emotional loss, blocked creativity, emptiness, closed heart
description: The Ace of Cups symbolizes new emotional beginnings, love, compassion, and spiritual awakening.
detailed_description: The Ace of Cups is the beginning card of the Cups suit (Water), symbolizing the opening of the heart, new love, and emotional abundance. A large cup, often overflowing with water or a fountain springing forth, is held by a hand emerging from a cloud. A dove (symbol of the Holy Spirit/peace) carries a host (communion). This offers a new beginning in love, friendship, creativity, or spiritual life. It's an invitation to receive love, compassion, and emotional joy. Its energy is about connection, intuition, and spiritual connection. In its reversed meaning, the cup may be spilled or sealed—indicating emotional loss, blocked creativity, feelings of emptiness, or rejection of love.

name: Two of Cups
meaning_up: Unity, partnership, connection, mutual attraction, harmonious relationship
meaning_rev: Breakup, imbalance, broken communication, disharmony
description: The Two of Cups represents partnership, connection, and the beginning of a meaningful relationship.
detailed_description: The Two of Cups depicts a man and woman exchanging cups, with the caduceus symbol (staff with winged serpents) above them, symbolizing harmonious unity and balance. This is a card of love, deep friendship, and balanced partnership. It indicates mutual attraction, understanding, and a supportive relationship. Could be the beginning of a romantic relationship, a strong business partnership, or reconciliation. Its energy is about unity and heart connection. In its reversed position, it indicates imbalance in relationships, separation, miscommunication, or lack of reciprocity.

name: Three of Cups
meaning_up: Celebration, friendship, community, social events, shared joy
meaning_rev: Overindulgence, gossip, isolation, third party intrusion
description: The Three of Cups represents celebration, friendship, and joyful social connections.
detailed_description: The Three of Cups shows three women dancing together, raising their cups in celebration. The background is full of abundant fruits and plants. This is a card of joy, friendship, and community. It marks celebrations, reunions, weddings, or simply happy times spent with supportive friends. Its energy is about sharing happiness, collective creativity, and social support. It reminds us of the importance of healthy social connections. In its reversed meaning, celebrations may become excessive (partying, alcohol), friendships may be disrupted by gossip, or feelings of isolation from the group.

name: Four of Cups
meaning_up: Apathy, contemplation, disconnection, boredom, introspection
meaning_rev: New opportunities, awareness, acceptance, breaking free
description: The Four of Cups represents contemplation, introspection, and feeling disconnected from emotions.
detailed_description: In the Four of Cups, a figure sits under a tree with three cups in front of them, and a fourth cup is offered by a hand from a cloud, but they don't see it, appearing bored or disconnected. This card symbolizes apathy, boredom, and contemplation. You may feel dissatisfied with what you have (three cups) and fail to see new opportunities (fourth cup) being offered. This is a time for introspection and seeking deeper meaning, but also a warning not to sink into indifference or daydreaming. In its reversed position, awareness of new opportunities emerges—you begin to accept offers, break out of the rut, or rediscover interest in life.

name: Five of Cups
meaning_up: Loss, grief, disappointment, sadness, mourning, regret
meaning_rev: Moving on, acceptance, finding peace, healing
description: The Five of Cups represents loss, grief, and focusing on what's been lost rather than what remains.
detailed_description: The Five of Cups shows a black-cloaked figure sadly looking at three spilled cups in front of them, while two cups still stand intact behind them. This is a card of sorrow, regret, and disappointment. The focus is on what has been lost (spilled cups), ignoring what remains and is still intact (the two cups behind). This represents a period of mourning a loss—relationship, opportunity, or dream. The sadness is valid, but this card also reminds us that not everything is lost. In its reversed meaning, this indicates the beginning of acceptance, finding peace, and finally being able to see what remains and move forward.

name: Six of Cups
meaning_up: Nostalgia, memories, childhood, innocence, joy, sweet memories
meaning_rev: Living in past, moving forward, letting go, maturity
description: The Six of Cups represents nostalgia, childhood memories, and innocent joy from the past.
detailed_description: The Six of Cups often depicts two children, where the older offers a cup of flowers to the younger, in a setting that looks like a childhood garden. This is a card of nostalgia, happy memories, and innocence. It could mean reunion with someone from the past, rediscovering simple joys, or being influenced by childhood experiences. Its energy is sweet and sentimental, inviting us to appreciate our roots and memories. However, it can also be a warning not to become too attached to the past. In its reversed position, it may mean being truly trapped in the past and refusing to move forward, or conversely—finally letting go of the past and looking ahead.

name: Seven of Cups
meaning_up: Choices, illusions, fantasy, imagination, wishful thinking, many options
meaning_rev: Clarity, decision-making, lack of options, reality check
description: The Seven of Cups represents choices, illusions, and being overwhelmed by too many options.
detailed_description: In the Seven of Cups, a figure sees seven cups floating in the clouds, each containing different enticements (such as a snake, castle, jewels, veiled head, etc.). This is a card of choices, fantasy, and illusion. You may be bombarded by many possibilities, dreams, or offers, but not all are real. Some are mirages. This card warns about daydreaming and decisions made based on illusion rather than reality. It encourages seeking clarity and focus before acting. In its reversed meaning, it may mean gaining clarity about which choices are real, finally making a decision, or feeling that no good options are available.

name: Eight of Cups
meaning_up: Walking away, disillusionment, searching, abandonment, leaving behind
meaning_rev: Stagnation, fear of change, avoidance, clinging
description: The Eight of Cups represents walking away from something that no longer serves you in search of deeper meaning.
detailed_description: The Eight of Cups shows a figure walking away from a neat stack of eight cups, heading toward mountains and darkness. The moon shines above. This is a card of emotionally 'leaving behind'. You realize that a situation, relationship, or material achievement (cups) no longer satisfies your soul. There is a call to seek deeper meaning, even if the journey is solitary and uncertain (toward darkness). This is an act of courage and spiritual seeking. In its reversed position, you may fear making this change, choosing to remain in an unsatisfying situation, or avoiding necessary inner searching.

name: Nine of Cups
meaning_up: Contentment, satisfaction, wish fulfillment, gratitude, emotional fulfillment
meaning_rev: Smugness, dissatisfaction, unmet expectations, arrogance
description: The Nine of Cups represents contentment, satisfaction, and having your wishes fulfilled.
detailed_description: Often called the 'wish card', the Nine of Cups shows a figure sitting contentedly in front of nine neatly arranged cups behind them. They look satisfied and happy. This is a card of emotional satisfaction, wish fulfillment, and gratitude. The things you've hoped for in terms of love, happiness, and personal fulfillment have been achieved. This is a time to enjoy the fruits of your emotional labor and feel grateful. However, there is also a hint of self-satisfaction. In its reversed meaning, satisfaction may turn into smugness and arrogance, or expectations may not be met, causing disappointment.

name: Ten of Cups
meaning_up: Harmony, marriage, happiness, alignment, family, emotional fulfillment
meaning_rev: Disconnection, misalignment, family conflicts, disharmony
description: The Ten of Cups represents emotional fulfillment, happy family life, and harmonious relationships.
detailed_description: The Ten of Cups depicts a family (often a couple with children) dancing happily under a rainbow with ten cups arching above them. This is a card of family happiness, harmony, and highest emotional fulfillment. It represents ideal love, a happy home, and the feeling that everything in life is aligned. It is the perfect conclusion to the emotional journey of the Cups suit. In a broader context, it may mean finding your inner 'home' or a community where you feel truly accepted and loved. In its reversed position, this harmony is disrupted—family conflicts, feelings of disconnection, or misalignment of values with loved ones.

name: Page of Cups
meaning_up: Creative opportunity, intuitive message, curiosity, dreamer, emotional exploration
meaning_rev: Creative block, emotional immaturity, insecurity, unrealistic dreams
description: The Page of Cups represents creative inspiration, intuitive messages, and emotional exploration.
detailed_description: The Page of Cups is the young messenger of the Water element. He stands by the sea, intently looking into his cup, from which a fish (symbol of the subconscious) emerges. He represents intuitive messages, creative inspiration that arises suddenly, and innocent emotional sensitivity. This could mean good news about feelings, the beginning of a sweet romantic attraction, or an invitation to explore your creative and emotional side. He is the dreamer and sensitive soul. In its reversed position, messages may be unclear or delayed, creativity is blocked, or it indicates emotional immaturity and insecurity.

name: Knight of Cups
meaning_up: Romance, charm, imagination, beauty, idealist, following heart
meaning_rev: Moodiness, disappointment, unrealistic expectations, illusion
description: The Knight of Cups represents romance, charm, and following your heart's desires.
detailed_description: The Knight of Cups is the romantic and charmer of the Water suit. As an elegant knight, he rides a calm horse, holding his cup as if offering love. He represents romantic feelings, artistic charm, and following the heart's call. He is a seeker of love and beauty, often idealistic and full of imagination. His arrival may signal a love offer, proposal, or a period where emotions and creativity are prioritized. However, he can also be too sentimental and lacking practicality. In its reversed meaning, his romanticism may turn into moodiness, easy disappointment, or unrealistic expectations about love and relationships.

name: Queen of Cups
meaning_up: Compassion, calm, comfort, intuition, emotional security, nurturing
meaning_rev: Martyrdom, insecurity, dependence, emotional manipulation
description: The Queen of Cups represents compassion, emotional security, and deep intuitive understanding.
detailed_description: The Queen of Cups is the highly intuitive and compassionate ruler of the Water element. Seated on her throne by the sea, holding her closed cup with both hands, she is contemplative and emotional. She is connected to the subconscious (sea) and has deep emotional understanding. She represents nurturing, empathy, and psychic sensitivity. She is a great listener and provides emotional comfort. In its reversed meaning, her compassion may turn into martyr mentality, unhealthy emotional dependence, deep insecurity, or using intuition to manipulate others' feelings.

name: King of Cups
meaning_up: Compassion, control, balance, diplomacy, emotional balance, leadership
meaning_rev: Emotional manipulation, moodiness, volatility, suppressed emotions
description: The King of Cups represents emotional mastery, compassion, and balanced leadership.
detailed_description: The King of Cups is the ruler who perfectly masters his emotions. Seated on his throne in the midst of rough seas (symbolizing strong emotions), but he remains calm and composed. A cup in one hand and a staff in the other indicates balance between heart and action. He represents someone compassionate, diplomatic, and with great self-control. He is an advisor, healer, or leader who leads with heart but still holds to principles. He shows that it's possible to feel deep emotions without being overwhelmed by them. In its reversed position, this balance is lost—he may become emotionally manipulative, moody, unstable, or suppress emotions until they explode.

name: Ace of Swords
meaning_up: Breakthrough, clarity, sharp mind, truth, mental clarity, decisive action
meaning_rev: Confusion, chaos, lack of clarity, misuse of intellect
description: The Ace of Swords represents mental clarity, truth, and breakthrough insights.
detailed_description: The Ace of Swords is the beginning of the Swords suit (Air), symbolizing mental power, truth, and intellectual breakthrough. A large sword held by a hand emerging from a cloud, often with a crown at its tip and olive/oak leaves symbolizing victory and wisdom. This sword cuts through confusion and illusion, bringing absolute clarity and undeniable truth. This could mean brilliant ideas, sudden insights, or the power to decide with clear thinking. However, the double-edged sword—truth can be painful but liberating. In its reversed meaning, this clarity is distorted—confusion, mental chaos, truth being misused, or inability to see clear solutions.

name: Two of Swords
meaning_up: Difficult choices, stalemate, blindness, blockage, decision paralysis
meaning_rev: Indecision, confusion, information overload, breakthrough
description: The Two of Swords represents difficult choices, indecision, and being at a crossroads.
detailed_description: The Two of Swords shows a woman seated with her eyes closed, holding two crossed swords over her chest. Behind her is a turbulent sea, but she appears calm. This card symbolizes deadlock, difficult choices, and refusal to see reality (eyes closed). You may feel stuck between two equally unappealing options, or refusing to make a decision for fear of consequences. This is a time to seek balance and clarity, but defensive posture (crossed swords) hinders this. In its reversed position, the deadlock begins to break—it could mean making a decision (however difficult), increasing confusion, or being overwhelmed by new information.

name: Three of Swords
meaning_up: Heartbreak, sorrow, grief, pain, separation, emotional wound
meaning_rev: Recovery, forgiveness, moving on, healing, acceptance
description: The Three of Swords represents heartbreak, emotional pain, and the experience of loss.
detailed_description: The Three of Swords is one of the saddest cards in the deck. Three swords pierce through a heart, often with dark clouds and rain in the background. This symbolizes heartbreak, sadness, and betrayal. The pain is sharp, clear, and involves feeling betrayed, abandoned, or deeply lost. This card acknowledges real emotional suffering. It is not a time to deny the pain, but to experience it fully as part of the healing process. In its reversed meaning, the swords begin to be pulled out—the healing process begins, forgiveness (for oneself or others) becomes possible, and the first steps toward moving on are taken.

name: Four of Swords
meaning_up: Rest, recuperation, meditation, solitude, contemplation, healing
meaning_rev: Restlessness, burnout, stress, lack of progress, exhaustion
description: The Four of Swords represents rest, recuperation, and taking time for mental restoration.
detailed_description: The Four of Swords shows a knight lying on an altar or bed, with three swords hanging on the wall and one beneath them. They are resting, perhaps after battle (Three of Swords). Stained glass windows often indicate spiritual peace. This card is a call to rest, retreat, and recover from mental pressure or conflict. It's a time for meditation, deep sleep, or temporarily withdrawing to regain mental clarity. This is not laziness, but necessary rest for healing. In its reversed position, this rest may be refused—exhaustion, restlessness, ongoing stress, or feeling trapped in inactivity.

name: Five of Swords
meaning_up: Conflict, tension, defeat, winning at all costs, power struggle
meaning_rev: Reconciliation, making amends, past resentment, forgiveness
description: The Five of Swords represents conflict, tension, and winning battles but losing the war.
detailed_description: In the Five of Swords, a figure stands arrogantly with three swords, while two other figures walk away defeated and sad. The remaining swords are scattered on the ground. This is a card of conflict where there are clear winners and losers, but the victory feels hollow and may damage relationships. It represents arguments, intimidation, or situations where someone wins at others' expense—'winning the battle, losing the war'. The feeling afterward is emptiness and isolation. This card warns about the price of unnecessary confrontation. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate efforts toward reconciliation, making peace with past conflict consequences, or releasing resentment.

name: Six of Swords
meaning_up: Transition, moving on, rite of passage, healing, progressive change
meaning_rev: Stagnation, resisting transition, unfinished business, delay
description: The Six of Swords represents transition, moving away from difficulty, and healing journeys.
detailed_description: The Six of Swords shows a figure and a child (or passenger) in a boat being rowed across calm waters toward a brighter side, with six swords embedded in the boat. The water behind is rough, ahead is calm. This symbolizes transition from difficult times to a more peaceful state. It is a healing journey, physical or emotional moving, and leaving problems behind. Although the journey may feel lonely (swords in the boat), there is hope ahead. This is a progressive card showing things will improve. In its reversed position, this transition may be delayed—refusal to move, stagnation, or carrying 'baggage' (swords) from the past that slows the journey.

name: Seven of Swords
meaning_up: Deception, trickery, tactics, strategy, avoidance, cunning
meaning_rev: Coming clean, rethinking approach, conscience, honesty
description: The Seven of Swords represents deception, trickery, and using cunning to achieve goals.
detailed_description: The Seven of Swords depicts a figure sneaking away from a camp, carrying five swords, leaving two swords stuck in the ground. Their expression is sly. This card symbolizes deception, evasion, and cunning tactics. Someone may be trying to 'get away with' something without being noticed, taking unethical shortcuts, or acting with hidden motives. This could be a warning to beware of others' deceit, or reflect our own tendency to avoid direct confrontation through trickery. In its reversed meaning, deception may be exposed, someone chooses honesty, or a cunning approach is being reevaluated due to guilt.

name: Eight of Swords
meaning_up: Restriction, imprisonment, victim mentality, self limitation, feeling trapped
meaning_rev: Self acceptance, new perspective, freedom, empowerment
description: The Eight of Swords represents restriction, self-imposed limitations, and feeling trapped by circumstances.
detailed_description: The Eight of Swords shows a woman bound and blindfolded, surrounded by eight swords stuck in the ground, trapped in her own mental 'prison'. However, the ground beneath is muddy and water is in the distance, and the bindings are not too tight—showing that liberation may be easier than it appears. This card symbolizes feeling trapped, limited by our own thoughts, fears, or limiting beliefs. It is a victim mentality and learned helplessness. The message is that we often become prisoners of our own minds, and the key is also in our minds. In its reversed position, it indicates beginning to accept oneself, gaining new perspective, and taking first steps toward mental freedom.

name: Nine of Swords
meaning_up: Anxiety, worry, fear, depression, nightmare, mental suffering
meaning_rev: Hope, reaching out, despair, trauma, seeking help
description: The Nine of Swords represents anxiety, worry, and mental anguish, often experienced during the night.
detailed_description: The Nine of Swords depicts someone sitting up in bed, covering their face with their hands, with nine large swords hanging on the wall behind them. This is a card of anxiety, excessive worry, and mental torment, often occurring at night when our minds are most restless. The fears may be unfounded or exaggerated, but the pain is very real. This card represents periods of depression, guilt, or nightmares. It is the peak of mental suffering in the Swords suit. In its reversed meaning, although still a difficult card, it may mean seeking hope, finally talking about worries, or beginning to address underlying trauma.

name: Ten of Swords
meaning_up: Betrayal, endings, loss, crisis, rock bottom, final blow
meaning_rev: Recovery, regeneration, resistance, new beginning
description: The Ten of Swords represents painful endings, betrayal, and hitting rock bottom.
detailed_description: The Ten of Swords is the dramatic and painful ending card of the Swords suit. A figure lies face down with ten swords piercing their back, dark sky above, but in the distance dawn is beginning to break. This symbolizes total betrayal, tragic ending, and feeling completely 'destroyed'. You may feel betrayed, defeated, or that the situation has ended very badly. However, the hidden message is: this is rock bottom, and the only way is up. The approaching dawn symbolizes new hope after total destruction. The pain is extreme, but it is finally over. In its reversed position, recovery may have already begun, or you are still fighting against an inevitable ending.

name: Page of Swords
meaning_up: Curiosity, restlessness, mental energy, vigilance, thirst for knowledge
meaning_rev: Deception, manipulation, gossip, all talk, intellectual arrogance
description: The Page of Swords represents curiosity, mental energy, and the pursuit of truth through questioning.
detailed_description: The Page of Swords is the young and clever messenger of the Air element. He stands on rocky ground with strong winds, holding his sword with both hands, ready to act or defend. He represents intellectual curiosity, restless mental energy, and vigilance. He is a truth-seeker, questioning, and sometimes skeptical. His arrival may bring news or ideas requiring sharp analysis. However, he can also be too argumentative or just 'all talk'. In its reversed position, this curiosity may be used to deceive, manipulate with words, spread gossip, or fail to turn ideas into action.

name: Knight of Swords
meaning_up: Action, impulsiveness, assertiveness, ambition, haste, mental speed
meaning_rev: Aggression, brutality, lack of planning, recklessness
description: The Knight of Swords represents swift action, ambition, and charging ahead with ideas.
detailed_description: The Knight of Swords is the ambitious and impulsive intellect knight of the Air suit. He rides at full speed with sword raised, ready to attack or charge forward. He represents quick mental action, ambition to win, and impatience. He is intelligent and determined, but can be too aggressive, harsh with words, and act without considering emotional consequences. His arrival brings rapid change and decisive decisions, but also confrontation. In its reversed meaning, this aggression becomes uncontrollable—cruelty, lack of planning leading to disaster, or actions completely hindered by obstacles.

name: Queen of Swords
meaning_up: Clarity, direct communication, truth, independence, intellectual sharpness
meaning_rev: Coldness, bitterness, harsh judgment, cruelty, cynicism
description: The Queen of Swords represents clarity, truth, and direct communication with intellectual sharpness.
detailed_description: The Queen of Swords is the highly intelligent and independent ruler of the Air element. Seated on her throne with sword raised upward in one hand, and the other hand raised, she is alert and clear. Her face shows life experience that has given her wisdom, perhaps through suffering. She represents mental sharpness, direct (even blunt) communication, and the ability to see objective truth without being hindered by emotions. She is independent, self-reliant, and analytical. In its reversed meaning, this clarity may become cold and cruel—becoming bitter, harshly judgmental, or using intellect to hurt others rather than seeking truth.

name: King of Swords
meaning_up: Intellectual power, authority, truth, clarity, command, sound judgment
meaning_rev: Manipulation, cruelty, weakness, tyranny, injustice
description: The King of Swords represents intellectual authority, truth, and clear judgment.
detailed_description: The King of Swords is the supreme ruler of the mental and intellectual realm. Seated on a stone throne with sword in his right hand (symbol of power and truth), he is the ultimate judge, leader, or strategist. He represents authority that comes from clear thinking, irrefutable logic, and the ability to make fair and impartial decisions. He is an expert in law, science, or military command. His justice is firm but ideally fair. In its reversed position, this mental power is used for evil purposes—manipulation with words, intellectual cruelty, tyranny, or showing weakness in decisions and judgment.

name: Ace of Pentacles
meaning_up: Opportunity, prosperity, new venture, abundance, material potential
meaning_rev: Missed opportunity, lack of planning, bad investment, stagnation
description: The Ace of Pentacles represents new financial or material opportunities, prosperity, and abundance.
detailed_description: The Ace of Pentacles is the beginning of the Pentacles suit (Earth), symbolizing new material opportunities, prosperity, and physical manifestation. A hand emerges from a cloud, holding a large Pentacle coin with a lush garden below. This offers the seed for worldly success—new job, investment, business, or improved health. It is a promise of growth and stability if you work the ground (work hard). Its energy is practical, grounded, and rooted. In its reversed meaning, this opportunity may be missed due to lack of attention or planning, poor investment, or an unfruitful beginning.

name: Two of Pentacles
meaning_up: Balance, adaptability, time management, priorities, juggling resources
meaning_rev: Disorganization, financial loss, overcommitting, imbalance
description: The Two of Pentacles represents balance, juggling priorities, and adapting to changing circumstances.
detailed_description: The Two of Pentacles shows a young man dancing or juggling two large coins tied with an infinity ribbon (lemniscate), while ships at sea behind him rise and fall with the waves. This is a card of adjustment, balance, and managing multiple responsibilities (often financial). Life feels like a juggling game, but with agility and humor, you can manage it. It's about flexibility and finding rhythm amid change. In its reversed position, balance is lost—chaos, financial loss, over-commitment, or inability to handle pressure.

name: Three of Pentacles
meaning_up: Teamwork, collaboration, learning, implementation, skilled work
meaning_rev: Lack of teamwork, disorganized, poor planning, unrecognized skills
description: The Three of Pentacles represents teamwork, collaboration, and skilled work coming together.
detailed_description: The Three of Pentacles depicts a craftsman (stonemason) working on a cathedral, discussing with two others (usually a monk and a noble) who hold plans. This is a card of skilled craftsmanship, collaboration, and recognition of talent. It represents working in a team to create something lasting and valuable, learning from more experienced people, and applying skills appropriately. It's a sign of hard work being rewarded and success through mastery. In its reversed meaning, it may indicate lack of cooperation, poor planning, careless work, or unrecognized skills.

name: Four of Pentacles
meaning_up: Conservation, security, frugality, control, possession, financial stability
meaning_rev: Greed, materialism, self-protection, release of control
description: The Four of Pentacles represents security, conservation, and holding tightly to what you have.
detailed_description: The Four of Pentacles shows a figure seated, tightly holding one coin above their head, one in each hand, and one under each foot. They sit in a prosperous city but look anxious. This card symbolizes financial security, conservation, and need for control. There is a strong desire for stability and protecting what has been acquired. However, too tight a grip can become greed, stinginess, or fear of change. It's about finding balance between security and generosity. In its reversed position, the grip may tighten further (becoming greedy) or actually loosen—releasing control, becoming more generous, or taking necessary financial risks.

name: Five of Pentacles
meaning_up: Need, poverty, isolation, worry, financial loss, hardship
meaning_rev: Recovery, charity, improvement, help, support
description: The Five of Pentacles represents financial hardship, poverty, and feeling excluded from support.
detailed_description: The Five of Pentacles depicts two poor and sick people walking in snow outside a brightly lit church window. They seem not to see the source of help nearby. This card symbolizes material difficulty, poverty, illness, and feelings of alienation from community or spiritual support. This is a time of lack and concern about basic needs. However, help is often available (the church), but invisible due to pride, arrogance, or despair. In its reversed meaning, it indicates the beginning of recovery from hardship, receiving charity, or gradual improvement in material circumstances.

name: Six of Pentacles
meaning_up: Charity, generosity, sharing, giving and receiving, balanced exchange
meaning_rev: Debt, selfishness, imbalance, strings attached, exploitation
description: The Six of Pentacles represents charity, generosity, and the balanced flow of resources.
detailed_description: The Six of Pentacles shows a wealthy merchant weighing and distributing coins to two beggars. The scales symbolize fairness and balance. This card is about generosity, charity, and giving as well as receiving. It may mean you are in a position to help others, or you are receiving help. It emphasizes the importance of sharing wealth and maintaining a healthy flow of resources in society. However, it's also about power dynamics in giving. In its reversed position, it may indicate debt, greed, imbalance in giving (e.g., giving with 'strings attached'), or exploitation.

name: Seven of Pentacles
meaning_up: Patience, reward, investment, long term view, perseverance, assessment
meaning_rev: Lack of reward, impatience, wasted effort, re-evaluation
description: The Seven of Pentacles represents patience, long-term investment, and waiting for rewards to grow.
detailed_description: The Seven of Pentacles depicts a farmer leaning on his tool, contemplating seven pentacles growing on a bush. He assesses his work and considers next steps. This card symbolizes patience, long-term investment, and waiting for the fruits of hard work. It's a period of evaluation—will your efforts bear fruit? Are you planting in fertile ground? It encourages persistence and belief that growth takes time. In its reversed position, impatience may arise, expected results don't materialize, or efforts may feel wasted, prompting you to reevaluate your strategy.

name: Eight of Pentacles
meaning_up: Apprenticeship, skill development, quality, craftsmanship, dedicated work
meaning_rev: Perfectionism, lack of ambition, low quality, careless work
description: The Eight of Pentacles represents skill development, craftsmanship, and dedicated work toward mastery.
detailed_description: The Eight of Pentacles shows a craftsman focused on carving eight coins in his workshop, ignoring the city in the distance. This is a card of dedication, skill development, and meticulous craftsmanship. It represents the apprenticeship stage, hard work to improve expertise, and pride in work quality. The focus is on the process, not the end result. It's about becoming a true 'craftsman' in your field. In its reversed position, this dedication may turn into excessive perfectionism, lack of ambition to grow, or producing poor and careless work.

name: Nine of Pentacles
meaning_up: Luxury, self-sufficiency, fruits of labor, independence, material comfort
meaning_rev: Self-worth, recklessness, financial loss, dependency
description: The Nine of Pentacles represents luxury, self-sufficiency, and enjoying the fruits of your labor.
detailed_description: The Nine of Pentacles depicts an elegant woman in her lush vineyard, with a falcon on her gloved hand. She is independent, prosperous, and enjoying material comforts achieved through hard work and discipline. This is a card of financial independence, luxury, and appreciation of natural beauty. She represents someone who has achieved success through their own efforts and can now relax and enjoy it. It's about balance between work and pleasure. In its reversed position, this independence may be disrupted by self-esteem issues, financial recklessness leading to loss, or hidden dependency.

name: Ten of Pentacles
meaning_up: Legacy, inheritance, family, establishment, wealth, long-term security
meaning_rev: Family conflict, instability, loss of inheritance, disconnection
description: The Ten of Pentacles represents legacy, family wealth, and long-term financial security.
detailed_description: The Ten of Pentacles depicts three generations of family in a prosperous and stable home setting, with ten Pentacle coins arranged on an archway. A dog (loyalty) and two pillars (stability) are often present. This is a card of inherited wealth, long-term financial security, and strong family foundations. It represents the highest achievement in material and social status. It's about creating a legacy, having deep roots, and enjoying the benefits of success built over generations. In its reversed position, this stability is threatened—family conflict, financial instability, or loss of inheritance.

name: Page of Pentacles
meaning_up: Ambition, desire, diligence, scholarship, opportunity, practical learning
meaning_rev: Lack of progress, procrastination, learn from failure, missed chance
description: The Page of Pentacles represents ambition, diligence, and the pursuit of practical goals.
detailed_description: The Page of Pentacles is the young and diligent messenger of the Earth element. He stands in a field, intently gazing at the Pentacle coin he holds. He represents messages or opportunities related to finances, education, or work. He is a diligent student, enthusiastic apprentice, or someone starting a new venture carefully. His energy is practical, ambitious, and focused on slow and steady growth. This is the beginning of the path toward material success. In its reversed position, messages or opportunities may be missed, progress hindered by procrastination, or a need to learn from practical failure.

name: Knight of Pentacles
meaning_up: Efficiency, routine, conservatism, reliability, hard work, methodical progress
meaning_rev: Laziness, boredom, stagnation, stubbornness, rigidity
description: The Knight of Pentacles represents reliability, hard work, and methodical progress toward goals.
detailed_description: The Knight of Pentacles is the slowest and most reliable of all the knights. He sits on a sturdy horse in a freshly plowed field, carefully holding his Pentacle coin. He represents hard work, persistence, and methodical progress. He is conservative, responsible, and not afraid of boring work. He is the one who gets things done. His arrival signals steady and reliable progress, but it may be slow. In its reversed meaning, this persistence may turn into laziness, boredom with routine, total stagnation, or stubbornness that refuses new methods.

name: Queen of Pentacles
meaning_up: Practicality, creature comforts, nurturing, financial security, domesticity
meaning_rev: Self-centeredness, jealousy, smothering, materialism, greed
description: The Queen of Pentacles represents practicality, nurturing, and creating material security and comfort.
detailed_description: The Queen of Pentacles is the practical and nurturing ruler of the Earth element. Seated on her throne in a lush garden, with a Pentacle coin in one hand, she is the guardian of home, health, and material resources. She represents nurturing through provision—food, shelter, financial security. She is connected to nature and finds joy in simple comforts. She is a kind and capable person who manages household or business with care. In its reversed meaning, these qualities may become distorted—self-centered, jealous of what others have, smothering nurturing, or excessive materialism.

name: King of Pentacles
meaning_up: Abundance, prosperity, security, achievement, leadership, financial mastery
meaning_rev: Authoritative, greedy, materialistic, indulgent, tyrannical
description: The King of Pentacles represents financial mastery, abundance, and material success through leadership.
detailed_description: The King of Pentacles is the supreme ruler of the material and financial world. Seated on a throne decorated with fruits and grapevines, with a Pentacle coin and staff in his hands, he is a successful entrepreneur, banker, or landowner. He represents prosperity, security, and achievement through discipline, smart work, and good leadership. He is reliable, generous with his wealth, and has the Midas touch—everything he touches flourishes. He is the foundation of a prosperous community. In its reversed position, his success may make him authoritarian, greedy, excessively materialistic, or engaged in excessive worldly pleasures.
